article.hook: You shrink away from sharp words in crowded rooms. Lilith slips into Pisces and the pain you can’t name becomes a secret refuge. Escape isn’t just an option - it’s the default setting for months.
article.lived: For about nine months, the world’s edge feels too jagged to touch. We pull back into quieter places, sometimes a little too quiet: a playlist that blurs time, a habit that numbs without notice, a story where we’re broken but safe. The wound sits beneath the skin, raw but invisible, making the day-to-day feel like walking on glass while pretending you’re barefoot on sand.
article.turn: The gift - deep imagination and real compassion - shifts when the escape becomes a shelter from choice. We replay the victim role until it’s a second skin, avoiding the sharpness of real decisions by dissolving into stories and distractions. The softer world wins by default; reality waits, ignored and unpaid for.
moves: Schedule one honest check-in that skips the usual excuses.
Write a letter you don’t intend to send, then burn it.
Set a timer to sit still with discomfort instead of scrolling or zoning out.
